feed.title: AMD Presents Latest High-Performance Computing Technologies in 2022 Product Premiere Livestream
feed.summary: AMD announced over 30 new products in its 2022 Product Premiere livestream, including Ryzen 6000 Series processors for notebooks, new Radeon RX 6000 Series GPUs for laptops and desktops, and the Ryzen 7 5800X3D desktop processor. The company also previewed its forthcoming Ryzen 7000 Series desktop processors based on the new "Zen 4" architecture. These releases aim to deliver leadership performance for productivity, content creation, and gaming experiences across various PC segments.

feed.title: An Under the Radar High Quality ETF
feed.summary: The Fidelity Quality Factor ETF (FQAL) received a five-star rating from CFRA, outperforming its peers and the S&P 500 in 2021 despite its smaller asset size. The fund focuses on free cash flow and return on invested capital with a sector-neutral approach, and CFRA expects it to continue outperforming. Eight of its top-10 holdings are considered undervalued by CFRA analysts.

feed.title: CORSAIR ONE i300 Compact PC Announced, powered by Intel Alder Lake, DDR5, RTX 3080 with a starting price of $3999.99 US
feed.summary: CORSAIR has announced their new ONE i300 compact form-factor desktop PC series, starting at $3999.99. These power-packed systems feature 12th Gen Intel Core i9-12900K CPUs, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080/3080 Ti GPUs, and CORSAIR's VENGEANCE DDR5 memory up to 64GB. Designed for gamers and creatives, the ONE i300 offers a 20% performance improvement over previous generations within a small 12-liter frame, stabilized by a patented convection-assisted liquid cooling system.

feed.title: John Deere’s New Autonomous Tractor Offers Timeliness, Efficiency, Quality of Life
feed.summary: John Deere has unveiled a fully autonomous tractor at CES 2022, set for production this year, to address labor shortages, improve farming efficiency, and enhance farmers' quality of life. The machine integrates advanced technologies like AI, machine learning, and GPS to allow 24/7 operation without an in-cab operator. Farmers can remotely monitor and manage the tractor via a mobile device, facilitating greater productivity and sustainability in agriculture.

feed.title: Qualcomm unveils ‘digital chassis’ tech at CES as it diversifies beyond smartphones
feed.summary: Qualcomm introduced its "digital chassis" strategy at CES, aiming to expand its mobile technology expertise beyond smartphones and into the automotive industry. This includes a new Snapdragon Ride Vision System for advanced driver assistance and infotainment deals with major car manufacturers like Volvo, Honda, and Renault. The company projects its automotive revenue to reach $3.5 billion annually in five years, signaling a significant diversification effort.

feed.title: HP OMEN reveals products for 2022, including the unique cooling device, the OMEN Cryo Chamber
feed.summary: HP OMEN has unveiled its 2022 gaming lineup, featuring the OMEN 45L Desktop with the innovative OMEN Cryo Chamber CPU cooling solution, which significantly lowers temperatures. The lineup also includes the OMEN 25L Desktop, the compact Victus by HP 15L Desktop, and the OMEN 27u 4K Gaming Monitor, designed for next-gen consoles. These new products offer advanced performance, cooling, and customization options for a diverse gaming audience.

feed.title: What Crypto-related ETFs Could Hit the US Market in 2022?
feed.summary: The article discusses the potential for various crypto-related ETFs, particularly metaverse products, to launch in the US market in 2022, while the approval of spot bitcoin and ether futures products remains uncertain. Industry experts express apprehension about the immediate investability of metaverse ETFs due to potential crossover in holdings and a lack of pure-play names. There's also skepticism regarding the SEC's approval of a spot bitcoin ETF in 2022, with some analysts expecting an ether futures-based ETF to gain approval sooner.

feed.title: GM will use Qualcomm chips in upcoming Ultra Cruise driver assistance system
feed.summary: General Motors has partnered with Qualcomm to develop its Ultra Cruise driver assistance system, which aims to enable vehicles to operate autonomously 95% of the time. The system will leverage Qualcomm's Snapdragon SA8540P systems-on-chip and an SA9000P AI accelerator, alongside a third-party microprocessor. This collaboration marks a significant expansion for Qualcomm into the automotive sector, where it projects substantial revenue growth, and positions it as a key competitor against Nvidia in the autonomous vehicle chip market.

feed.title: Nvidia’s Omniverse ‘metaverse for engineers’ emerges from beta
feed.summary: Nvidia's Omniverse, a "metaverse for engineers" designed for 3D simulation and design collaboration, is now generally available for free to Nvidia Studio creators with GeForce RTX gear after a successful public beta. The platform offers new creative features, including AI-enabled 3D face modeling animation and is being utilized by companies like Ericsson to optimize 5G network buildouts by modeling signal propagation in virtual cities. Omniverse leverages Nvidia's RTX GPU technology and Pixar's Universal Scene Description for real-time collaboration and simulation across various industries.

feed.title: CES 2022: HP shows off Elite Dragonfly G3, Dragonfly Chromebook and lots more new hardware
feed.summary: At CES 2022, HP unveiled a comprehensive portfolio targeting the hybrid-work market, including the Elite Dragonfly G3, Dragonfly Chromebook, and several new monitors, laptops, and desktop PCs. The new Elite Dragonfly G3 is a premium ultraportable laptop with a 13.5-inch screen and 12th-gen Intel Core processors, while the Dragonfly Chromebook offers a Chrome OS alternative with unique features like a haptic trackpad. HP also introduced various conferencing and webcam monitors, updated EliteBook and ProBook business laptops, and new desktop PCs and curved displays for creators.

feed.title: Innoviz Technologies unveils third-generation LiDAR sensor
feed.summary: Innoviz Technologies has introduced its third-generation LiDAR sensor, the Innoviz360, building on its previous successful products. This new sensor offers high-resolution, a wide field of view, and reduced cost, aiming to overcome existing limitations in fully autonomous vehicles (L4-L5) like robotaxis and trucks. The company also expects the Innoviz360 to open new market opportunities beyond automotive, including logistics, mapping, and smart infrastructure, with samples anticipated in Q4 2022.

feed.title: Leading HPC Software Company Bright Computing Joins NVIDIA
feed.summary: Bright Computing, a leading HPC software company with over 700 customers, has been acquired by NVIDIA. This acquisition integrates Bright Cluster Manager into NVIDIA's accelerated computing software stack, aiming to simplify the building and operation of HPC data centers. The partnership will enhance NVIDIA's DGX and data center businesses and support the growing trend of industrial HPC by making advanced computing more accessible.

feed.title: Nvidia buys high-performance computing cluster management software provider Bright Computing
feed.summary: Nvidia has acquired Bright Computing Inc., a company specializing in software for managing high-performance computing (HPC) systems. This acquisition aims to enhance Nvidia's offerings in the HPC market, integrating Bright's Cluster Manager into Nvidia's software stack to provide more complete infrastructure platforms for accelerated computing. The move is seen as another step in Nvidia's evolution from a chip company to a comprehensive solution provider for data centers, particularly as HPC and AI workloads converge.

feed.title: AI Startup Speeds Up Derivative Models for Bank of Montreal
feed.summary: Riskfuel, a Toronto-based AI startup, has partnered with Bank of Montreal (BMO) to accelerate its derivative models using NVIDIA DGX systems. This technology significantly improves the performance of complex financial calculations, enabling BMO to make faster and more accurate investment decisions and expand its client base. Riskfuel's solution allows banks to run derivative portfolio models in seconds, offering both speed and accuracy.

feed.title: Stellar December gives TSMC record year
feed.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) reported record sales for the previous year, driven by strong demand for its advanced 5-nanometer process used in emerging sectors like 5G and high-performance computing. The company's consolidated sales reached NT$1.59 trillion ($57.47 billion USD), an 18.5 percent increase from 2020. TSMC is expected to announce a significant capital expenditure budget for the current year to further expand production capacity and maintain its technological advantage.

feed.title: Corsair One i300 gaming PC review
feed.summary: The Corsair One i300 is a compact, high-end gaming PC featuring Intel's Core i9 12900K, an Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 Ti, and 64GB of DDR5-4800 RAM, priced at $4,999. It delivers excellent 4K gaming performance and operates quietly due to its unique liquid cooling system, though the CPU can run hot under heavy load. The article praises its aesthetic and hardware-packed design, acknowledging its high cost but highlighting its cutting-edge components and quiet operation.

feed.title: HP Spectre x360 16 (2021) review: A high-quality 16-inch convertible with a superb OLED screen
feed.summary: The HP Spectre x360 16 (2021) is a 16-inch convertible laptop featuring an 11th-gen Intel Core i7 processor and discrete Nvidia GeForce RTX 3050 graphics, along with a stunning UHD+ OLED touchscreen. While it offers powerful performance and excellent audio, its 2.01kg weight makes it unwieldy in tablet mode, and the 512GB SSD is considered insufficient for its premium price. The battery life is moderate, offering about 6 hours of mixed use before needing a recharge.

feed.title: NVIDIA Named America’s Best Place to Work on Latest Glassdoor List
feed.summary: NVIDIA has been ranked as America's best place to work on Glassdoor’s 14th annual Best Places to Work list for large U.S. companies in 2022. The ranking is based on anonymous employee feedback, with 95% of NVIDIA employees recommending the company and 98% approving of CEO Jensen Huang. This recognition highlights NVIDIA's commitment to employee satisfaction amid evolving workplace expectations.

feed.summary: TSMC, the world's largest chip etcher, continues to be a highly profitable enterprise, consistently investing ahead of demand and achieving strong financial results. TSMC is also advancing its manufacturing processes with new variants of its 5 nanometer node and the upcoming 3 nanometer node, with significant investments planned for these advanced technologies.

feed.title: Serve Robotics achieves autonomous robo-delivery milestone
feed.summary: Serve Robotics has achieved a significant industry milestone by completing the first-ever commercial deliveries using Level 4 autonomous vehicles that require zero human intervention. The company's robots are equipped with advanced sensors and AI computing to navigate autonomously, drastically reducing the need for remote operators. This achievement marks a major advancement in robotic delivery, bringing the industry closer to fully autonomous operations in various environments.

feed.title: Chip giant Nvidia expands R&D operations in Israel
feed.summary: Nvidia is expanding its R&D operations in Israel by establishing a new design and engineering group focused on next-generation CPUs for AI, robotics, and autonomous vehicles. The company, which acquired Israel's Mellanox Technologies in 2020, plans to hire additional engineers in Israel, further solidifying the country's role as Nvidia's largest R&D hub outside the US. This expansion intensifies competition for tech talent in Israel, where both Nvidia and Intel have significant R&D presence, and Google is also entering the chip-making sector.

feed.title: Nvidia expands Israel R&D operations
feed.summary: Nvidia is expanding its R&D operations in Israel by establishing a new design and engineering group to develop next-generation CPUs. The company plans to hire hundreds of Israelis for this initiative, adding to its existing 2,800 employees across seven locations in the country. This expansion reinforces Israel's role as a key player in Nvidia's global tech ecosystem, including its DPU development and AI research, and builds upon its acquisition of Mellanox.

feed.title: Israeli quantum cryptographic solutions provider QuantLR integrates with NVIDIA
feed.summary: Israeli company QuantLR, a provider of quantum cryptographic solutions, has integrated its technology with NVIDIA's networking suite. This collaboration aims to develop quantum-secured data centers and accelerate the deployment of affordable quantum encryption solutions. QuantLR's CEO, Shlomi Cohen, highlighted the importance of NVIDIA's support in advancing their technology against eavesdropping and hacking attempts, anticipating significant growth in the quantum encryption market.

feed.title: Van, Go: Pony.ai Unveils Next-Gen Robotaxi Fleet Built on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin
feed.summary: Pony.ai, a self-driving startup, has announced its next-generation autonomous computing platform built on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin. This platform will power a robotaxi fleet of Toyota Sienna MPVs, marking a significant step for the company in developing level 4 self-driving vehicles. The high-performance, energy-efficient AI compute platform is designed for scalable autonomous driving development, with road testing beginning in China this year and commercial rollout planned for 2023.

feed.title: Pony.ai Achieves Development Milestone with New Autonomous Computing Unit Built on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin
feed.summary: Pony.ai has developed a new autonomous computing unit built on the NVIDIA DRIVE Orin system-on-chip, marking a significant move towards automotive-grade hardware for mass production. This development will accelerate the deployment of Pony.ai's Level 4 autonomous capabilities, with production set for late 2022. The system features high performance and reliability, and its scalable design will support both self-driving trucks and robotaxis.

feed.title: In Its Next Significant Milestone for L4 Robotaxis, Pony.ai Debuts Its 6th Generation Autonomous Driving System Design
feed.summary: Pony.ai has unveiled its 6th generation autonomous driving system, designed for L4 automotive-grade mass production fleets, featuring advanced sensors and NVIDIA DRIVE computing platforms. The first vehicle equipped with this system, a Toyota Sienna Autono-MaaS (S-AM), will begin road testing in China in 2022 and join Pony.ai's public robotaxi operations in early 2023. This system aims to enhance safety, reliability, and cost-effectiveness for large-scale robotaxi deployment, incorporating a 23-sensor suite and an NVIDIA DRIVE Orin-powered computing unit.

feed.title: Serve Robotics Launches First Level 4 Self-Driving Delivery Robots
feed.summary: Serve Robotics has announced the launch of its Level 4 self-driving delivery robots, marking a significant milestone in autonomous vehicle technology. These robots can operate without human intervention, relying on their onboard systems to navigate urban environments safely. This achievement, resulting from five years of development and partnerships with NVIDIA and Ouster, enables widespread robotic delivery and enhances public safety by reducing human error.

feed.title: Intel to invest at least $20 billion in Ohio chip-making facility
feed.summary: Intel Corp. plans to invest at least $20 billion in a new chip-making facility near Columbus, Ohio, to bolster its semiconductor production in response to increased demand for digital products and a global chip shortage. This investment is part of Intel's broader strategy to expand its manufacturing capabilities and regain its position as a leading chip designer and manufacturer, including for other companies. The move is expected to create 3,000 permanent jobs in Ohio and comes at a time when governments are offering subsidies to attract semiconductor production plants to reduce supply-chain disruptions.

feed.title: Intel is building a $20 billion computer chip facility in Ohio amid a global shortage
feed.summary: Intel announced a $20 billion investment to construct two computer chip factories in central Ohio, aiming to alleviate the ongoing global semiconductor shortage. This move is expected to create thousands of jobs and enhance U.S. chip manufacturing capacity, reducing reliance on Asian producers. The project is Ohio's largest single private-sector investment, with production anticipated to begin by the end of 2025.

feed.title: Intel investing $20 billion to bring chip manufacturing to Ohio amid global shortage
feed.summary: Intel announced an investment of over $20 billion to build two new semiconductor chip factories in central Ohio. This project aims to address the global chip shortage and reduce the U.S.'s reliance on Asian manufacturing for semiconductors. The initiative is expected to create 3,000 Intel jobs and 7,000 construction jobs, with production slated to begin in 2025.

feed.title: Nvidia powers latest Pony.ai autonomous car platform
feed.summary: Pony.ai, an autonomous driving technology company, has chosen Nvidia's Drive Orin SoC for its sixth-generation autonomous driving system. This platform is designed to enable mass production of Level-4 autonomous vehicles, with trials set to begin in China this year using Toyota's S-AM vehicle, followed by deployment in Pony.ai’s robotaxi operations in H1 2023. Nvidia's chip can process 254 trillion operations per second.

feed.title: Low-power AI computer chip startup Ceremorphic exits stealth with $50M funding
feed.summary: Ceremorphic Inc., a startup focused on energy-efficient AI supercomputing chips, has emerged from stealth mode with a $50 million Series A funding round. The company, founded by tech veteran Dr. Venkat Mattela, aims to develop a "complete silicon system" incorporating a 5-nanometer processor with a unique architecture and patented multithread technology (ThreadArch) to address reliability, security, and energy consumption challenges in high-performance AI, HPC, and metaverse applications. The funding for the Series A round was entirely provided by the company's founders, many of whom have a background with Redpine Signals Inc., known for ultralow-power wireless chipsets.

feed.title: CES 2022 Recap: Tech Becoming More Accessible and Interoperable
feed.summary: CES 2022 showcased significant advancements making technology more accessible and interoperable. Key trends included enhanced immersion in the metaverse with new AR/VR products, traditional auto OEMs committing to mass-market electric vehicles, and the emergence of a unified Internet of Things ecosystem through initiatives like Matter. The event highlighted a shift towards practical, everyday applications for emerging technologies, signaling potential disruptions in various sectors.

feed.title: What a Bristol-Myers project to monitor off-label prescribing says about future uses of A.I.
feed.summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb collaborated with Cortical.io to utilize AI for monitoring off-label drug prescribing by analyzing social media data. The pilot project successfully identified off-label uses of drugs, including an unexpected finding for Suboxone, demonstrating the potential of natural language processing and less data-intensive AI methods for post-market surveillance. This initiative highlights the growing importance of AI in patient safety and the value of brain-inspired AI research.

feed.title: Nvidia preparing to walk away from Arm acquisition - Bloomberg News
feed.summary: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to abandon its $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd from SoftBank Group Corp, citing regulatory hurdles. The deal has faced scrutiny from U.S., British, and EU regulators concerned about potential anti-competitive effects. SoftBank is now reportedly stepping up preparations for an initial public offering (IPO) of Arm.

feed.title: Is chip giant Nvidia going to scrap its $40BN bid for Arm?
authors: Giles Turner and Peter Elstrom and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to abandon its $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. due to fierce regulatory backlash and little progress in securing approvals. Regulators and customers, including the U.S. FTC, have expressed concerns that the deal would make Nvidia too powerful. SoftBank, Arm's current owner, is stepping up preparations for an Arm initial public offering as an alternative.

feed.title: KU team wins valuable time on supercomputer to research improved aerodynamics
feed.summary: A team led by University of Kansas aerospace engineering professor Z.J. Wang has been awarded significant time on the Summit supercomputer at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. This award, part of the Department of Energy's INCITE program, provides 590,000 "node hours" worth millions of dollars in commercial value. The team will use this powerful computing resource to research improved aerodynamics for aircraft, specifically focusing on complex turbulent flows in high-lift configurations, a challenge considered critical for next-generation aircraft development.

feed.title: Nearly 80 Percent of Financial Firms Use AI to Improve Services, Reduce Fraud
feed.summary: A survey by NVIDIA reveals that 78% of financial services professionals use accelerated computing for AI-enabled applications, driving innovation across the industry. Fraud detection, conversational AI, and algorithmic trading are key use cases, with significant year-over-year growth in AI adoption for various applications. Despite challenges like budget constraints and a shortage of data scientists, executives view AI as critical for future business success, with focuses on hiring AI experts, identifying new use cases, and investing in infrastructure.

feed.title: Corsair One i300 Review: Power Packed In
feed.summary: The Corsair One i300 is a compact gaming PC that offers powerful performance with high-end components like an Intel Core i9-12900K and Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 Ti in a 12-liter chassis. While it provides big performance in a small package, making it ideal for limited desk space, its small size sacrifices some upgradeability and comes at a premium price, starting at $3,799.99 and reaching $4,999.99 as tested. The review highlights its strong gaming and productivity performance, outperforming larger systems in some benchmarks.

feed.title: Chip shortage to last six months, one year or 18 months-- depending on who’s talking
feed.summary: The article discusses the varying predictions for how long the global chip shortage will last, with estimates ranging from six months to 18 months or longer. It highlights views from IDC, Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger, and Texas Instruments, alongside ongoing efforts by the U.S. Congress and Commerce Secretary to address the issue through funding and incentives for domestic chip production. The consensus indicates that while some improvements might be seen, the shortage is expected to persist through 2022 and potentially into 2023 for various sectors.

feed.title: TSMC: Can anything stop Taiwan's chipmaking giant?
feed.summary: TSMC, the world's largest contract chip manufacturer, reported bumper financial results in late 2021, with revenue of $15.7bn and profits of $6bn. The company plans to invest $40-$44bn into capital expenditure to maintain its market dominance, dwarfing its rivals. Despite its strong position, TSMC faces challenges from competitors like Intel and Samsung, as well as geopolitical risks and the complexities of global expansion.

feed.title: AMD's stellar report fuels chip stock rally
feed.summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) reported strong quarterly demand for its semiconductors, boosting its annual revenue forecast and surpassing analysts' expectations, which led to an almost 11% surge in its stock. This positive report ignited a rally in other chip stocks, with Nvidia, Qualcomm, and Micron Technology also seeing jumps in their share prices, despite ongoing global supply snags and volatility in the semiconductor sector. Intel, however, saw a decline in its stock.

feed.title: Metaverse stocks Nvidia and Roblox fall as Facebook parent Meta's Web3 business reports massive loss
feed.summary: Shares of metaverse-related companies like Roblox, Nvidia, and Matterport fell after Meta Platforms reported a significant operating loss of $10 billion in its Web3 division, Reality Labs, for 2021. The news led to a market value wipeout of over $200 billion for Meta and a sell-off across various tech stocks connected to the metaverse concept. This downturn highlights concerns following Meta's aggressive push into the metaverse space.

feed.title: Chip giants are ramping up spending by the billions as semiconductor demand booms
feed.summary: Major semiconductor companies like TSMC and Intel are investing billions into new fabrication plants and research to meet the booming global demand for chips, despite the ongoing chip shortage. TSMC plans to spend $100 billion over three years, while Intel announced a $20 billion investment in Arizona. Analysts expect a "choppy" recovery from the shortage in the short term, but demand is projected to continue increasing, benefiting suppliers like ASML and Applied Materials.

feed.title: Chip Startup Ceremorphic Seeks AI, HPC Edge With New 5nm Design
feed.summary: Ceremorphic, a chip startup, has emerged from stealth mode with plans to produce a scalable, low-energy processor for AI and high-performance computing using TSMC's 5-nanometer process node. The company's CEO, Venkat Mattela, emphasizes that access to this advanced manufacturing process, secured through his team's prior success, as well as Ceremorphic's proprietary technologies for efficiency, reliability, and security, will set its Hierarchical Learning Processor apart from competitors. The startup aims to deliver samples to customers in 2023 and begin production in 2024, following test chip validation in March.

feed.summary: Nvidia Corp. has surpassed Meta Platforms Inc. to become the seventh-largest U.S. company by market value. This shift highlights Nvidia's rapid growth over the past few years and Meta's recent decline, which saw its market value drop by $267 billion since Wednesday's close.

feed.title: Nvidia’s $40bn takeover of UK chip designer Arm collapses
feed.summary: Nvidia's $40bn takeover of UK chip designer Arm has collapsed due to insurmountable regulatory hurdles, leading Arm to pursue a stock market flotation instead. The deal, which had been valued as high as $75bn, faced fierce opposition and regulatory scrutiny in multiple regions, including the US, UK, and China. Softbank will now prepare Arm for an IPO and receive a $1.25bn break-up fee from Nvidia.

feed.title: Doomed from the start? Why Nvidia failed to buy Arm from SoftBank
feed.summary: Nvidia's attempt to acquire Arm from SoftBank has failed due to significant regulatory challenges and widespread opposition from various stakeholders. Critics, including tech giants and regulators, raised concerns about job security, tech sovereignty, and access to Arm's chip designs. SoftBank now plans to list Arm on the stock market in 2023, with discussions ongoing about the listing location.

feed.title: SoftBank’s sale of Arm to Nvidia collapses, Arm to IPO
feed.summary: The proposed sale of Arm Ltd by SoftBank Group Corp to U.S. chipmaker Nvidia Corp has collapsed due to regulatory hurdles and scrutiny from various international bodies. Instead of the sale, which was valued at up to $80 billion, Arm will now plan for an initial public offering (IPO). The deal faced opposition from U.S., British, EU, and Chinese regulators over concerns about competition, pricing, and innovation in vital chip markets.

feed.title: Nvidia to withdraw from acquisition of SoftBank’s Arm
feed.summary: Nvidia is abandoning its US$40 billion acquisition of British semiconductor design firm Arm from SoftBank due to significant regulatory opposition. SoftBank now plans to pursue an initial public offering for Arm, expected by March 2023. Arm's CEO, Simon Segars, has resigned, with Rene Haas taking over.

feed.title: Relief and challenges for chipmakers as Nvidia-Arm megadeal collapses
feed.summary: The chip industry is reportedly relieved after the collapse of Nvidia's planned acquisition of Arm, a deal valued at up to $80 billion, which faced significant regulatory hurdles and geopolitical concerns. Despite the relief concerning Arm's neutrality, both companies now confront challenges that the merger aimed to address, particularly in expanding into the booming data center market. Arm is now planning an IPO in 2023, having previously argued that an IPO might force a focus on short-term profits over long-term strategic growth.

feed.title: What Nvidia Can’t Buy, It Can Still Get Through An Arm Partnership
feed.summary: Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Holdings from SoftBank Group was terminated due to regulatory scrutiny and market resistance, resulting in a $1.25 billion hit for Nvidia. Despite the failed acquisition, Nvidia, an Arm architecture licensee, plans to release its Arm server chip "Grace" next year and may pursue a joint venture partnership with Arm, allowing it to license its GPU and network chip technologies through Arm's licensing machine. The article suggests that such a partnership could enable many of the benefits Nvidia sought through ownership without the regulatory hurdles.

feed.title: The biggest chip merger ever is dead. Here's why Nvidia dropped its bid for Arm and what's next.
feed.summary: Nvidia's $40 billion planned acquisition of Arm has been called off due to significant concerns and opposition from its announcement. As a result, SoftBank now intends to take Arm public through an IPO. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that the company will continue to license architecture from Arm despite the deal's collapse.

feed.title: Collapse of Nvidia-Arm $66B Chip Deal Shows More Than Antitrust Woes
feed.summary: The $66 billion Nvidia-Arm chip deal collapsed due to "significant regulatory challenges," marking the end of a merger attempt initiated in September 2020. While antitrust concerns were prominent among regulators in the U.S., Europe, and the U.K., the article suggests that growing fears among policymakers about national security and access to essential chip technology played a more substantial role. This highlights a trend where national security interests, not just antitrust, are increasingly influencing regulatory decisions in the semiconductor industry.

feed.title: Nvidia’s Arm deal: Largest-ever chip merger terminated over ‘significant regulatory challenges’
feed.summary: Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Limited, which would have been the largest chip merger in history, has been officially terminated due to significant regulatory challenges globally. SoftBank, Arm's parent company, will retain a $1.25 billion breakup fee from Nvidia and plans to take Arm public by March 2023. Analysts suggest the termination is a "plus" for Arm, allowing it to maintain impartiality as an IP purveyor, and while a "setback" for Nvidia, it won't derail its progress in AI.

feed.title: We should never have sold Arm in the first place, says ALEX BRUMMER
feed.summary: Alex Brummer argues that the 2016 sale of British chip designer Arm Holdings to Japan's Softbank for £23 billion was a "serious betrayal" of British technology. He criticizes former Prime Minister Theresa May's government and Cabinet Secretary Jeremy Heywood for facilitating the deal, which he views as short-sighted given Softbank founder Masayoshi Son's intent to use Arm as a bargaining chip rather than for long-term investment. Brummer suggests that following the collapse of Nvidia's £50 billion bid for Arm, the British government has an opportunity to correct past mistakes and bring Arm back to the UK as a public company.

feed.title: Nvidia, SoftBank Call Off Blockbuster Arm Deal - WSJ
feed.summary: Nvidia and SoftBank have abandoned their $40 billion deal for Nvidia to acquire chip-design specialist Arm due to significant regulatory antitrust concerns. SoftBank, which owns Arm, now plans to pursue a public listing for the U.K.-based chip business. Nvidia will take a $1.36 billion charge against earnings related to the deal's termination, and SoftBank will retain the $1.25 billion prepaid by Nvidia.

feed.title: ETF of the month: VanEck Semiconductor UCITS ETF (SMGB)
feed.summary: The VanEck Semiconductor UCITS ETF (SMGB) has been named ETF of the month, highlighting its impressive performance in 2021 by returning 44.4% and gathering $859m in assets since its December 2020 launch. The ETF has benefited from increased demand for semiconductor chips driven by global digitalization, the reopening of economies, and emerging technologies like electric vehicles and 5G. Despite some recent market concerns from hedge fund selling, the semiconductor industry is projected to see continued revenue growth in 2022.

feed.title: Will Cisco Buy Splunk? Big Tech Bids $20 Billion on Public Company
feed.summary: Cisco Systems has reportedly offered $20 billion to acquire software company Splunk, aiming to expand its presence in the software industry. The potential acquisition faces regulatory hurdles and comes as Splunk navigates a leadership transition and business model shifts. Both companies' stocks reacted differently to the news, with Cisco's stock slightly down and Splunk's significantly up due to investor sentiment regarding financial backing.

feed.title: AMD Completes $49B Xilinx Acquisition, Largest Chip Deal In History
feed.summary: AMD has finalized its $49 billion acquisition of Xilinx, making it the largest chip deal in history and transforming AMD into an "industry’s high-performance and adaptive computing leader." This strategic move expands AMD's offerings beyond CPUs and GPUs into reprogrammable FPGAs, significantly boosting its presence in data centers, embedded computing, and telecommunications. The deal will also enhance AMD's total addressable market and is expected to be accretive to margins, earnings per share, and free cash flow in the first year.

feed.title: Lisa Su named AMD chair after completing $49B acquisition of Xilinx
feed.summary: Lisa Su has been named the chair of AMD following the completion of its $49 billion acquisition of Xilinx. This strategic move expands AMD's market focus, with the company estimating the value of its newly targeted markets to exceed $135 billion. The acquisition and promotion of Su highlight AMD's aggressive growth strategy in the semiconductor industry.

feed.title: AMD Closes Xilinx Deal: First Products Expected in 2023
feed.summary: AMD has completed its acquisition of Xilinx, a move expected to significantly expand AMD's presence in the datacenter sector by combining CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs. The first processors integrating Xilinx technologies are anticipated in 2023, showcasing a rapid integration compared to AMD's previous acquisitions. This merger aims to create a high-performance and adaptive computing leader, offering a comprehensive portfolio across cloud, edge, and intelligent devices.

feed.title: AMD Closes Record Chip Industry Deal with about $50-Bln Purchase of Xilinx
feed.summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) has finalized its acquisition of Xilinx Inc. for approximately $50 billion, making it a record deal in the chip industry. This acquisition allows AMD to expand into the cloud, edge, and intelligent devices market, intensifying its competition with Intel Corp. in the data center chip sector. The combined entity will be led by AMD CEO Lisa Su and aims to leverage an outsourced manufacturing strategy, primarily with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (TSMC).

feed.title: Intel Buying Tower Semiconductor for $5.4 Billion to Boost Supply Chain Capacity
feed.summary: Intel is acquiring Tower Semiconductor for $5.4 billion to expand its manufacturing capacity and strengthen its Intel Foundry Services (IFS) division. This acquisition is a key part of Intel's IDM 2.0 strategy, aiming to boost supply chain resilience and compete with leading chip manufacturers like TSMC. Tower Semiconductor will provide Intel with access to high-growth markets and enhance the scale of its foundry operations, which Intel believes is crucial for accelerating the growth of IFS.

feed.title: Intel to Buy Israel’s Tower Semiconductor for $5.4 Billion
feed.summary: Intel Corp. has agreed to acquire Israel’s Tower Semiconductor Ltd. for $5.4 billion as part of CEO Pat Gelsinger’s strategy to expand into the outsourced chip-manufacturing business. This acquisition aims to enhance Intel's expertise and customer base in the chip-foundry market, directly competing with industry leaders like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. The deal is expected to close in about 12 months and is a key part of Intel's broader investment cycle to modernize its factories and rebuild manufacturing capabilities.

feed.title: How to Not Stress About Tech
feed.summary: The article discusses how investors can avoid stressing over the tech sector's current volatility by being selective and focusing on quality companies. It highlights the Goldman Sachs Innovate Equity ETF (GINN) as an example of a fund that invests in profitable, cash-generating tech firms with strong competitive advantages, distinguishing them from “pandemic losers.” The piece emphasizes that while some pandemic-driven tech trends are fading, long-term secular growth themes persist, making selective tech investments still attractive.

feed.title: Jaguar Land Rover, Nvidia ally in vehicle software arms race
feed.summary: Luxury automaker Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has partnered with Nvidia to develop advanced computer brains and software for its vehicles launching from 2025 onwards. This collaboration aims to accelerate JLR's in-vehicle software development, enabling features like autonomous driving and parking, and providing more digital functions to drivers. The deal is a significant win for Nvidia in expanding its automotive industry presence and helps JLR compete with rivals like Tesla in digital technology.

feed.title: Jaguar Land Rover Announces Partnership With NVIDIA
feed.summary: Jaguar Land Rover has partnered with NVIDIA to develop next-generation automated driving systems and AI-enabled services for its future vehicles, starting in 2025. All new Jaguar and Land Rover models will be built on the NVIDIA DRIVE™ software-defined platform, integrating advanced safety features, driver assistance, and in-car AI functionalities. This collaboration aims to transform Jaguar Land Rover into a digital powerhouse by leveraging NVIDIA's AI expertise and full-stack solutions like DRIVE Hyperion and DGX for training AI models.

feed.title: Nvidia Posts Record Sales Amid Broad Chip Demand
feed.summary: Nvidia Corp. reported record quarterly sales of $7.64 billion, a 53% increase from the previous year, and projected further growth. The graphics-chip maker also more than doubled its net income to $3 billion, surpassing Wall Street expectations for both profit and sales. This strong performance comes amidst broad chip demand, despite the company moving past its failed takeover bid for Arm Ltd.

feed.title: Nvidia provides strong revenue outlook on demand for computer chips
feed.summary: Nvidia reported strong fiscal fourth-quarter earnings and a robust outlook for the current quarter, driven by exceptional demand for its chips in AI and other intensive applications. The company exceeded analyst expectations for both EPS and revenue, with data center sales up 71% and gaming up 37%. CEO Jensen Huang noted easing supply constraints and a projected substantial increase in product supply in the second half of 2022, despite the automotive business experiencing a decline and the Arm acquisition falling through previously.

feed.title: Nvidia reports record Q4, FY21 revenue on strong data center growth
feed.summary: Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $7.64 billion for Q4 FY21, a 53% increase year-over-year, and record fiscal year 2021 revenue of $26.91 billion, up 61% YoY, primarily driven by strong growth in its Data Center, Gaming, and Professional Visualization businesses. Data Center revenue alone saw a 71% YoY increase due to increased AI adoption, with the company anticipating continued growth in this sector, particularly with its new AGX Orin processor for autonomous vehicles and robotics. While acknowledging ongoing supply chain issues, Nvidia expects improvements and has expanded its supply chain for FY23, despite recently terminating its $40 billion acquisition deal with Arm Limited due to regulatory resistance.

feed.title: The Processor Chip Industry Is Another Ugly Capitalist Oligopoly
feed.summary: This article criticizes the semiconductor industry, labeling it as an "ugly capitalist oligopoly" due to the extreme concentration of chip manufacturing among a few companies, primarily Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). It highlights how this concentration, driven by high capital costs for fabrication plants and state subsidies, leads to supply chain vulnerabilities, inflation, and limited competition. The author argues that even efforts by governments like the US to subsidize domestic chip production won't fundamentally alter the industry's oligopolistic structure or shift its profit-driven nature.

feed.title: New Chips from Infineon, TI, and Toshiba Drive Advances in Autonomous Driving
feed.summary: As the autonomous vehicle market grows more competitive, new microcontroller units (MCUs) and integrated circuits (ICs) from Infineon, Texas Instruments (TI), and Toshiba are emerging to support advanced driver-assist systems (ADAS) functionalities. Infineon's AURIX TC4x series offers a heterogeneous architecture for automotive E/E systems and AI, while TI's AWR2944 radar sensor meets NCAP standards for improved traffic safety. Toshiba's TC9563XBG Ethernet bridge IC enables high-speed communication up to 10 Gbps and supports Zone Architectures in next-generation vehicles.

feed.title: CLSE ETF Profile: Dividends, Returns (CBOE:CLSE)
feed.summary: The Convergence Long/Short Equity ETF (CLSE) provides long and short exposure to mainly large- and mid-cap US stocks using a quantitative and fundamental ranking process. The fund aims for long-term capital growth with minimized volatility, targeting a monthly rebalance. CLSE, which was formerly a mutual fund, launched on February 22, 2022, and has assets under management of $748.13 million.

feed.title: Nvidia is set to spend at least $10B to secure its share of limited 5nm chip supply
feed.summary: Nvidia is reportedly planning to spend at least $10 billion to secure a significant share of TSMC's limited 5nm chip supply for its upcoming Ada Lovelace GPUs (RTX 40 series). This substantial investment is crucial for Nvidia to potentially achieve higher clock speeds and better power efficiency, giving them a competitive edge over rivals like AMD. The move highlights the intense competition among fabless companies for advanced chip manufacturing capacity, with Nvidia having already spent $9 billion on inventory and prepayments in a recent quarter.

feed.title: Industry's 1st Automotive-Qualified Switches Enable Autonomous Driving Ecosystem
feed.summary: Microchip Technology Inc. has launched the market's first Gen 4 automotive-qualified PCIe switches, including Switchtec PFX, PSX, and PAX solutions. These switches are designed to provide high-speed, low-latency connectivity for Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), which are crucial for next-generation autonomous driving applications. This development, a result of collaboration with technology partners like NVIDIA, addresses the need for robust interconnect capabilities in distributed computing systems within the automotive industry.

feed.title: Like building the world's tallest tower every two years
feed.summary: This article delves into the critical role of Intel Israel's Core Group in developing the most essential parts of Intel's processors: the cores. It explains the evolution of processor cores from single-core to multi-core designs, highlighting the challenges and innovations, including the creation of hybrid architectures with Performance and Efficiency Cores in the Alder Lake processor. The piece emphasizes the immense complexity and continuous innovation required in core development, likening it to building and constantly improving the world's tallest tower.

feed.title: Texas Instruments Inc. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
feed.summary: Texas Instruments Inc. stock experienced a slight drop of 0.03% on a generally grim trading day for the market. Despite this loss, the company's shares outperformed major indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, which fell more significantly. Texas Instruments also performed better than several of its competitors, with a trading volume exceeding its 50-day average.

feed.title: Veritas NetBackup 10, IBM FlashSystem Cyber Vault And Rambus HBM3
feed.summary: This article discusses key announcements from Veritas, IBM, and Rambus in the technology sector. Veritas introduced NetBackup 10, an evolution in cloud-based data protection with enhanced features. IBM unveiled its FlashSystem Cyber Vault and new FlashSystems, while Rambus detailed its HBM3 high-performance memory.

feed.title: An Interview with Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger
feed.summary: This article features an interview with Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger, discussing his IDM 2.0 strategy, the acquisition of Tower Semiconductor, and Intel's role in the semiconductor industry. Gelsinger explains why Intel is committed to manufacturing its own chips despite the success of fabless competitors, emphasizing the geopolitical importance of a Western technology provider and the benefits of integrating foundry operations. He also addresses concerns about potential overcapacity in the industry and the future of x86 architecture.

feed.title: Behind Intel’s HPC Chip that Will Pierce the Exascale Barrier
feed.summary: Intel has unveiled new details about its Ponte Vecchio processor, which will power the Aurora supercomputer, aiming to achieve exascale performance. The chip utilizes advanced 2D and 3D chiplet integration technologies, combining over 100 billion transistors across 47 pieces of silicon using various manufacturing processes, including TSMC's N5 and Intel 7. This heterogeneous integration and sophisticated thermal management are crucial for achieving the targeted 2 exaflops for the Aurora supercomputer.

feed.title: Qualcomm Inc. stock rises Friday, still underperforms market
feed.summary: Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) stock rose 1.76% on Friday, closing at $170.93, despite underperforming the broader market. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both saw larger gains. Qualcomm's stock remains below its 52-week high and showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Alphabet Inc. Cl A, NVIDIA Corp., and Cisco Systems Inc.

feed.title: Semiconductor sales to Russia banned, but that shouldn’t hurt Intel, AMD and other chip makers
feed.summary: Semiconductor companies are banning sales to Russia in response to its invasion of Ukraine. Despite a broader market sell-off and sanctions against Russia, an analyst believes these bans will have little financial impact on major chip makers like Intel and AMD because Russia's semiconductor market is likely too small to significantly affect their revenue.

feed.title: Use WGMI to Enter the Crypto Economy
feed.summary: The crypto economy is diversifying beyond direct Bitcoin ownership, with new ETFs like the Valkyrie Bitcoin Miners ETF (WGMI) offering access. WGMI focuses on bitcoin mining equities and is actively managed, allowing it to adapt to a nascent asset class with high growth potential. The ETF also incorporates a renewable energy overlay for its mining components, addressing environmental concerns associated with bitcoin mining.

feed.title: Nvidia says employee, company information leaked online after cyber attack
feed.summary: U.S. chipmaker Nvidia Corp reported a cyber attack that led to the leak of employee credentials and some proprietary company information online. The company became aware of the breach on February 23rd and is analyzing the leaked data, stating it does not anticipate business disruption. A ransomware group named "Lapsus$" has reportedly claimed responsibility for the leak, which is said to include schematics, drivers, and firmware for Nvidia's graphics chips.

feed.title: Nvidia Confirms Company Data Was Stolen in Hack
feed.summary: Nvidia has confirmed that data, including employee credentials and proprietary information, was stolen during a recent hack by the group LAPSUS$. While Nvidia states there's no evidence of ransomware or connection to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, LAPSUS$ claims to have acquired 1TB of data, including source code for DLSS technology, which they are now leaking online and attempting to sell. Nvidia does not anticipate business disruption as a result of the incident.

feed.title: Microsoft Corp Chief Satya Nadella’s son passes away
feed.summary: Zain Nadella, the 26-year-old son of Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and his wife Anu, passed away on Monday morning. Born with cerebral palsy, Zain's journey profoundly influenced Satya Nadella's focus on designing accessible products at Microsoft. The Children's Hospital, where Zain received treatment, collaborated with the Nadella family to establish the Zain Nadella Endowed Chair in Pediatric Neurosciences.

feed.title: Nvidia hackers allegedly attempting to blackmail company into open-sourcing GPU drivers
feed.summary: The Lapsus$ ransomware gang, responsible for a recent attack on Nvidia, is allegedly attempting to blackmail the company into open-sourcing its GPU drivers. The attackers have threatened to leak sensitive GPU files if Nvidia does not comply with their demands by a set deadline, which also included a previous request to remove mining hashrate limiters. Nvidia has confirmed a cybersecurity incident where employee credentials and proprietary information were stolen, but denies ransomware deployment.

feed.title: ST claims first 0.5-MP depth image sensor
feed.summary: STMicroelectronics has launched VD55H1, the first product in its new family of 0.5-megapixel indirect time-of-flight (iToF) sensors. This sensor offers high-resolution 3D depth imaging, targeting applications in smartphones for enhanced camera features and face authentication, as well as robotics and AR/VR for precise 3D scene mapping. The VD55H1 boasts low power consumption and high measurement accuracy, leveraging ST's unique pixel architecture and 40-nm stacked wafer technology.

feed.title: GLOBALFOUNDRIES ANNOUNCES NEXT GENERATION IN SILICON PHOTONICS SOLUTIONS AND COLLABORATES WITH INDUSTRY LEADERS TO ADVANCE A NEW ERA OF MORE IN THE DATA CENTER
feed.summary: GlobalFoundries (GF) has announced GF Fotonix™, its next-generation silicon photonics platform, aimed at addressing the explosive growth of data and reducing power consumption in data centers. GF is collaborating with industry leaders including Broadcom, Cisco Systems, Inc., Marvell, and NVIDIA, along with photonic innovators like Ayar Labs and PsiQuantum, to deliver innovative and feature-rich solutions. This monolithic platform, combining advanced photonics features and RF-CMOS on a single silicon wafer, is designed to enable faster, more energy-efficient data transmission and supports various high-growth markets.

feed.title: Nvidia invests $10M in sidewalk robot delivery company Serve Robotics
feed.summary: Nvidia has invested $10 million in Serve Robotics, an Uber spinout specializing in sidewalk delivery robots. This investment marks Nvidia's first foray into the sidewalk delivery sector and is part of a broader collaboration to advance robotic technology. Serve Robotics will use the funds to expand its service beyond Los Angeles and San Francisco, leveraging Nvidia's Jetson AI platform, perception, and mapping tools to enhance its fully autonomous delivery robots.

feed.title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split, $10 bln share buyback
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. has announced a 20-for-1 stock split and authorized a $10 billion share buyback plan, causing its shares to rise by 7% in extended trading. This marks Amazon's first stock split since 1999, aimed at making shares more accessible to investors and increasing flexibility for employees managing equity. Trading with the new share price will commence on June 6.

feed.title: Vodafone investigating threat from hackers behind Samsung breach to leak source code
feed.summary: Vodafone is investigating claims by the hacking group Lapsus$ that they have obtained 200 gigabytes of the telecommunication giant's source code and are threatening to leak it. The company is working with law enforcement and states that the repositories referenced typically contain proprietary source code, not customer data. Lapsus$ recently claimed responsibility for data breaches at Samsung and Nvidia.

feed.title: Why Nvidia sees a future in software and services: Recurring revenue
feed.summary: Nvidia is shifting its business model to focus on software and services to generate recurring revenue, moving beyond its traditional hardware sales. CFO Colette Kress highlighted opportunities in autonomous vehicles, where Nvidia's software will be monetized over the life of the car, and the metaverse, envisioning annual revenues of $1,000 per creative user and per digital twin bot. This strategic pivot aims to create more predictable income streams, leveraging existing hardware with new software offerings and expanding into new markets.

feed.title: Nvidia invests USD 10 million in Serve Robotics
feed.summary: Nvidia has invested $10 million in Serve Robotics, a company specializing in sidewalk delivery robots. This investment follows Serve Robotics' expanded seed round in December 2021 and will help the startup broaden its services beyond Los Angeles and San Francisco. Serve's robots utilize Nvidia's Jetson edge AI platform for autonomous movement and will integrate Nvidia's perception and mapping tools, alongside synthetic data generation for testing.

feed.title: Micron CEO says chip shortage improving, but could last into 2023
feed.summary: Micron Technology CEO Sanjay Mehrotra stated that the semiconductor shortage, which has affected numerous industries, is improving but could extend into 2023. He highlighted the automotive sector as particularly impacted, with modern vehicles becoming "data centers on wheels" that require significant memory and storage. Mehrotra emphasized the need for a partnership between the U.S. government and the private sector to establish the U.S. as a leader in the chip industry, noting that Micron plans to invest over $150 billion globally in memory manufacturing, research, and development.

feed.title: Nvidia investing $10M in last-mile company Serve Robotics
feed.summary: Nvidia is investing $10M in Serve Robotics, a last-mile delivery company that spun out of Uber. Serve Robotics utilizes Nvidia's Jetson edge compute module for its autonomous mobile robots, making this investment a continuation of their long-standing partnership. The funding will support Serve Robotics' expansion and fleet building in existing and new markets.

feed.title: Metaverse Technology Redefining Digital Experience
feed.summary: The metaverse is emerging as a significant technological advancement, moving beyond gaming to redefine digital experiences across various industries. Aptos is building its own open-source blockchain for Web3 applications and expects to launch its public mainnet in the third quarter of 2022.

feed.title: Serve, Nvidia Formalize Partnership with $10M Investment
feed.summary: Serve Robotics announced a $10 million strategic investment from chipmaker Nvidia, deepening their partnership and accelerating Serve's growth and development. This investment is significant as it's Nvidia's largest direct investment in a partner company in recent years and its first in the food robotics space. The collaboration aims to speed up the adoption and development of robots, especially as Serve Robotics recently achieved Level 4 automation, allowing robots to operate routinely without human intervention.

feed.title: New Investments Ready to Propel AV Technology Forward
feed.summary: New investments are rapidly advancing autonomous vehicle (AV) technology, with major automakers and tech companies pouring billions into R&D to enhance safety and performance. While full autonomy and mass adoption are long-term goals due to testing, regulatory, and infrastructure challenges, early commercial applications like robotaxis present immediate growth opportunities. The article details technological advancements, investment trends, regulatory hurdles, consumer acceptance, and the potential for AVs to revolutionize transportation.

feed.title: When the world runs low on neon gas
feed.summary: The Russia-Ukraine war has significantly impacted the global supply of neon gas, which is crucial for semiconductor manufacturing. Ukraine, home to two major neon purification companies, has halted production due to the conflict, threatening to exacerbate the existing worldwide chip shortage. This situation highlights the precarity of specialized global supply chains, where the disruption of a single component can have far-reaching consequences for the technology industry, leading to higher prices, delivery delays, and potential product unavailability.

feed.title: Is It Finally Time to Start Buying Intel Stock?
feed.summary: Intel, a pioneer in micro-processing, has seen its stock underperform competitors for years, but an ambitious makeover and new leadership may signal an attractive entry point for long-term investors. CEO Pat Gelsinger's plans for a massive $20 billion semiconductor plant in Ohio and other investments aim to restore Intel's market leadership. Despite investor skepticism reflected in its depressed stock price, Morningstar analysts see an appealing opportunity with a 27% discount to its fair value estimate and a 3.11% dividend yield.

feed.title: Nvidia unveils new technology to speed up AI, launches new supercomputer
feed.summary: Nvidia has unveiled new chips and technologies including the H100 chip, Grace CPU Superchip, and the "Eos" supercomputer, aimed at accelerating artificial intelligence algorithms and enhancing data center performance. These innovations are expected to significantly reduce AI model training times from weeks to days. The company is also focusing on monetizing its software business and sees the automotive sector as a key growth driver, projecting $11 billion in automotive business pipeline over the next six years.

feed.title: NVIDIA Introduces Grace CPU Superchip
feed.summary: NVIDIA has introduced its Grace CPU Superchip, an Arm-based data center CPU designed for AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. It features 144 Arm cores, 1 terabyte per second memory bandwidth, and an estimated performance of 740 on the SPECrate benchmark, consuming only 500 watts. The Grace CPU Superchip is expected to be available in the first half of 2023, enhancing applications across HPC, AI, and data analytics.

feed.title: Nvidia CEO lays out plans after Arm deal fell through, reveals new Hopper GPU
feed.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang unveiled the new Hopper GPU architecture, including the H100 chip, at the company's annual developer conference. This announcement marks Nvidia's first major public plan reveal since the Arm deal fell through, demonstrating the company's unchanged roadmap for GPUs and server CPUs. The new architecture, developed by TSMC, will initially be deployed in server configurations before expanding to other formats.

feed.title: Driving on Air: Lucid Group Builds Intelligent EVs on NVIDIA DRIVE
feed.summary: Lucid Group announced at GTC that its current and future electric vehicles, including the Lucid Air and upcoming Project Gravity SUV, are built on the NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion platform. This integration enables programmable, intelligent capabilities and allows for continuous over-the-air software updates, enhancing systems like the DreamDrive Pro advanced driver assistance system. The partnership ensures Lucid vehicles can incorporate the latest AI technology, providing improved features throughout the car's lifecycle.

feed.title: Lucid Announces Integration of Its Proprietary DreamDrive Pro Advanced Driver-Assistance System with NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion Software-Defined Platform
feed.summary: Lucid Group has announced that its DreamDrive Pro advanced driver-assistance system (ADAS) will integrate new features built on the NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion software-defined platform. This platform is already part of every Lucid Air vehicle and features a sophisticated 32-sensor suite, gigabit ethernet networking, and over-the-air software updates. The collaboration with NVIDIA aims to enhance DreamDrive Pro's capabilities, delivering continuous improvements and a future-ready customer experience through software updates.

feed.title: Nvidia debuts next-generation H100 GPUs, its most powerful chips yet
feed.summary: Nvidia has unveiled its next-generation H100 GPUs, built on the new Hopper architecture, which promise an order of magnitude performance improvement over previous models. These chips feature 80 billion transistors, a Transformer Engine for accelerating AI language models, and HBM3 memory. The H100 GPUs are designed for advanced AI workloads, including real-time inference, and will be available to customers and cloud providers in the third quarter.

feed.title: NVIDIA Launches AI Computing Platform for Medical Devices and Computational Sensing Systems
feed.summary: NVIDIA has introduced Clara Holoscan MGX, an AI computing platform designed for the medical device industry to develop and deploy real-time AI applications at the edge, adhering to regulatory standards. This platform expands the existing Clara Holoscan framework, offering a medical-grade reference architecture and long-term software support. It aims to accelerate innovation in medical devices by enabling real-time insights from high-throughput data streams for applications like robotic surgery and drug discovery.

feed.title: Keynote Wrap-Up: Turning Data Centers into ‘AI Factories,’ NVIDIA CEO Intros Hopper Architecture, H100 GPU, New Supercomputers, Software
feed.summary: During NVIDIA GTC, CEO Jensen Huang unveiled a vision of data centers as "AI Factories," introducing the new Hopper GPU architecture and H100 GPU, along with new AI and accelerated computing software. He also announced powerful new data-center-scale systems, including Grace CPU Superchip and DGX H100 supercomputers. Huang emphasized the role of Omniverse in integrating real and virtual worlds, speeding collaboration, and serving as a proving ground for new robotics and autonomous vehicles.

feed.title: Siemens Gamesa Taps NVIDIA Digital Twin Platform for Scientific Computing to Accelerate Clean Energy Transition
feed.summary: Siemens Gamesa is collaborating with NVIDIA to develop physics-informed digital twins of wind farms using NVIDIA Omniverse and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. This digital twin platform for scientific computing aims to optimize wind farm layouts, increase electricity production, and reduce operating costs by enabling faster and more accurate simulations of computational fluid dynamics, up to 4,000 times quicker than traditional methods. The technology will help analyze and minimize wake effects between turbines, accelerating the clean energy transition.

feed.title: NVIDIA Announces DGX H100 Systems – World’s Most Advanced Enterprise AI Infrastructure
feed.summary: NVIDIA has announced its fourth-generation DGX H100 systems, which are the world's first AI platforms built with the new NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, offering 32 petaflops of AI performance. These systems are foundational for the next-generation DGX POD and DGX SuperPOD AI infrastructure, with the latter able to deliver 1 exaflop of AI performance. NVIDIA is also building the "Eos" supercomputer, which is expected to be the world's fastest AI system with 18.4 exaflops of AI computing performance, set to begin operations later this year.

feed.title: NVIDIA Introduces Grace CPU Superchip
feed.summary: NVIDIA has unveiled its Grace CPU Superchip, an Arm Neoverse-based discrete data center CPU engineered for AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. This new chip boasts 144 high-performance cores and 1 terabyte/second memory, offering double the performance and energy-efficiency compared to current leading server chips. It is designed to work seamlessly with NVIDIA's existing software stacks and is expected to be available in the first half of 2023.

feed.title: NVIDIA Opens NVLink for Custom Silicon Integration
feed.summary: NVIDIA has announced the opening of NVLink-C2C, an ultra-fast chip-to-chip and die-to-die interconnect, for custom silicon integration. This technology allows coherent interconnection between custom dies and NVIDIA's GPUs, CPUs, and DPUs, offering significant improvements in energy efficiency and area efficiency compared to PCIe Gen 5. It supports industry standards like Arm AMBA CHI and will also be compatible with the developing Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) standard, providing options for custom silicon integration with NVIDIA chips.

feed.title: NVIDIA Launches Data-Center-Scale Omniverse Computing System for Industrial Digital Twins
feed.summary: NVIDIA has introduced OVX, a new computing system designed to power large-scale industrial digital twins within its Omniverse platform. OVX combines high-performance GPU-accelerated compute, graphics, and AI with fast storage and networking to create physically accurate simulations for complex applications. This system will enable industries to build and test digital twins of factories, cities, and railway networks, and is expected to be available later this year through partners like Inspur, Lenovo, and Supermicro.

feed.title: NVIDIA Announces Availability of Jetson AGX Orin Developer Kit to Advance Robotics and Edge AI
feed.summary: NVIDIA has announced the availability of its Jetson AGX Orin developer kit, a powerful AI supercomputer designed for advanced robotics, autonomous machines, and edge computing. This new kit offers over eight times the processing power of its predecessor, the Jetson AGX Xavier, while maintaining a compact form factor. NVIDIA expects the Jetson AGX Orin to accelerate the development of next-generation robotics and edge AI products across various industries, supported by a broad ecosystem of partners and customers.

feed.title: Lucid Announces Integration of Its Proprietary DreamDrive Pro Advanced Driver-Assistance System with NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion Software-Defined Platform
feed.summary: Lucid Group announced the integration of its DreamDrive Pro advanced driver-assistance system with NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion software-defined platform. This collaboration ensures that DreamDrive Pro will gain new capabilities over time through over-the-air software updates, leveraging NVIDIA's powerful compute architecture. The system, featuring a 32-sensor suite, is already integrated into every Lucid Air and is designed for future enhancements.

feed.title: NVIDIA Launches Omniverse for Developers: A Powerful and Collaborative Game Creation Environment
feed.summary: NVIDIA has launched new Omniverse features for developers, creating a powerful and collaborative environment for game creation. This update streamlines game development by integrating AI and NVIDIA RTX tools, enabling real-time collaboration and enhancing character animation and asset management. Key new features include Omniverse Audio2Face, Omniverse Nucleus Cloud, Omniverse DeepSearch, and an Unreal Engine 5 Omniverse Connector.

feed.title: NVIDIA Announces Hopper Architecture, the Next Generation of Accelerated Computing
feed.summary: NVIDIA has announced its next-generation accelerated computing platform, NVIDIA Hopper architecture, featuring the new H100 GPU with 80 billion transistors. This architecture delivers an order of magnitude performance leap over its predecessor, the Ampere architecture, and includes groundbreaking features such as a Transformer Engine and scalable NVLink for advanced AI models. The H100, designed for "AI factories," is expected to be available later this year from leading cloud service providers and computer makers.

feed.title: NVIDIA DRIVE Continues Industry Momentum With $11 Billion Pipeline as DRIVE Orin Enters Production
feed.summary: NVIDIA's DRIVE Hyperion platform, powered by DRIVE Orin, is gaining significant industry momentum with an $11 billion automotive pipeline. Leading EV maker BYD and several self-driving startups have selected the DRIVE Hyperion architecture for their next-generation software-defined vehicles, with DRIVE Orin now in production. The platform enables advanced autonomous driving capabilities and supports the development of new energy vehicles.

feed.title: Introducing NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion 9: Next-Generation Platform for Software-Defined Autonomous Vehicle Fleets
feed.summary: NVIDIA announced DRIVE Hyperion 9, its next-generation open platform for automated and autonomous vehicles, set to launch in 2027. This scalable and programmable architecture will leverage the DRIVE Thor central computer, offering 8x the performance of current platforms. DRIVE Hyperion 9 features heightened sensing capabilities with a rich array of high-resolution cameras, radars, lidars, and ultrasonics, designed for Level 3 urban and Level 4 highway driving.

feed.title: This tech group is leading the charge in sustainable Web 3.0 development
feed.summary: Atlas Technology Management, a Singapore-headquartered technology group, is expanding its Web 3.0 computing infrastructure and committing to sustainable development. The company aims to achieve 100% green energy adoption by 2024 and plans to expand its global coverage to over 30 countries in the next five years. Atlas is also exploring advanced technologies like underwater data centers to minimize environmental impact.

feed.title: Nvidia CEO says interested in exploring chip manufacturing with Intel
feed.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed interest in exploring Intel's chip manufacturing services. Intel, which aims to expand its foundry business, confirmed ongoing discussions with Nvidia. This potential collaboration could be significant for Intel's efforts to attract external chip design companies to its factories.

feed.title: Kroger partners with Nvidia to boost freshness efforts using AI
feed.summary: Kroger has announced a strategic collaboration with Nvidia to enhance its fresh food initiatives using artificial intelligence and online simulations. The partnership will establish a lab and demonstration center at Kroger's headquarters to develop AI-driven methods for identifying food spoilage, optimizing delivery routes, and improving in-store efficiency. This move aims to leverage technology to extend the shelf life of fresh produce and improve customer service, aligning with Kroger's "Fresh for Everyone" branding.

feed.title: Kroger launches ambitious AI transformation program
feed.summary: Kroger is launching an ambitious AI transformation program through a partnership with Nvidia, aiming to enhance enterprise operations. This initiative includes building an AI lab and demonstration center to improve freshness initiatives, shipping logistics, and store experiences using digital twin simulations. Kroger will also leverage technologies like computer vision and dynamic routing for last-mile delivery, building on its existing AI-driven fulfillment model with Ocado.

feed.title: Possible Nvidia, Intel GPU Alliance Could Frustrate Rivals AMD, TSMC
feed.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is in talks with Intel to use its foundries for GPU production, a move that could significantly impact competitors AMD and TSMC. This potential alliance would diversify Nvidia's supply base and challenge TSMC's dominance in the foundry market, while also putting pressure on AMD's supercomputing ambitions. Both Intel and Nvidia are interested in the collaboration, with Intel aiming to become the top GPU foundry by 2025.

feed.title: Nvidia considers teaming up with Intel on chip manufacturing
feed.summary: Nvidia is in discussions with Intel about potentially using Intel as a foundry for manufacturing its chips. This consideration comes amid a global semiconductor chip shortage and Intel's efforts to become a major U.S. foundry supplier, despite the challenges of aligning technologies and business models between the companies. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed openness to the idea, noting existing close collaboration between the firms.

feed.title: 16-year-old living with his mom is Lapsus$ mastermind behind Microsoft hack, cyber detectives say
feed.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have traced a string of hacks against major technology companies like Microsoft, Nvidia, and Okta to a 16-year-old living with his mother near Oxford, England. This teenager, known online as "White" and "breachbase," is believed to be the mastermind behind the Lapsus$ hacking group, which has engaged in social engineering and extortion campaigns, often taunting victims and recruiting insiders. The group, which Microsoft tracks as "DEV-0537," is known for its poor operational security, allowing researchers to gain insights into its members who also include a suspected teenager in Brazil.

feed.title: SoftBank preps Arm IPO, seeking a $60B valuation
feed.summary: SoftBank is preparing for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Arm Ltd., aiming for a $60 billion valuation, following the collapse of its proposed sale to Nvidia Corp. The valuation is considered ambitious but potentially realistic due to Nvidia's appreciating stock price since the original acquisition agreement. Analysts suggest the success of the IPO at this valuation could indicate investor confidence in Arm's own growth potential beyond a merger.

feed.title: WeRide zooms to $400m
feed.summary: China-based autonomous driving technology producer WeRide has raised $400 million from investors including GAC and Robert Bosch, bringing its valuation to $4.4 billion. This latest funding round increases the company's total funding to over $1.2 billion and follows previous rounds with notable investors such as Alliance Ventures and Nvidia GPU Ventures. WeRide, founded in 2017, develops software and hardware for level 4 autonomous driving.

feed.title: Columbia Threadneedle Investments launches Columbia Seligman Semiconductor and Technology ETF
feed.summary: Columbia Threadneedle Investments has launched its first actively managed, semi-transparent ETF, the Columbia Seligman Semiconductor and Technology ETF (SEMI). Managed by Paul Wick and his team, SEMI focuses on growth within the semiconductor and related technology sectors, investing in 30 to 50 companies. The fund aims to capitalize on the critical role of semiconductors in modern technologies and offers investors exposure to a sector believed to be reasonably valued with strong potential for future returns.

feed.title: TIME100 Most Influential Companies 2022: NVIDIA
feed.summary: NVIDIA, under CEO Jensen Huang, has become critical for various technologies from cryptocurrency to self-driving cars, earning it a spot on the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies list. Despite abandoning a major acquisition, NVIDIA's investments in AI and experimental technology are profoundly shaping the future, with expectations for its processors to make human effort obsolete in many sectors.

feed.title: TIME100 Most Influential Companies 2022: NVIDIA
feed.summary: NVIDIA has been recognized as one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies of 2022 due to its essential role in advancing technology. Under CEO Jensen Huang, NVIDIA's processors are crucial for cryptocurrency, NFTs, and self-driving cars. The company's investments in AI and experimental technology are significantly shaping the future, despite abandoning a major acquisition this year.
